by_theme.definition: A name misdescribes what a value holds or a function does, is vague, lacks a verb, or omits a type suffix (*_id, is_*).
A new type, wrapper, function, flag, check or special case the goal does not need; a simpler design exists.
The reviewer rejects, redirects or specifies the design or product behaviour; judging it needs product context.
Wording of user-facing or model-facing product copy, as distinct from its length.
A clarifying question with no correction implied.
What a record stores and how: identity, derivable or duplicate fields, one shape versus several, persistence layout.
Coined jargon, a synonym for an existing concept, or an overloaded or banned word where the project already has a word.
Prose (prompt, tool description, doc, comment) longer than its content needs.
Code sits in the wrong module or layer, or a layer knows app or domain concepts it should not.
Code, fields or branches that nothing reads or can reach.
The agent did not do what was asked or agreed, deferred it, or reintroduced something rejected.
Prose states something untrue, overclaims, frames the point wrong, or does not parse.
Work given to the LLM, or a rule left in prompt prose, that code or schema should derive or enforce.
One fact, list, rule or approach is kept in two places that must agree.
A logic error, missed edge case, unmet real-world requirement, or a workaround instead of the root cause.
Validation, None-handling or raising is misplaced or missing: Optional deferral, missing guard, soft return, broad except.
dict[str, Any], Any or an untyped dict where a model with named fields belongs.
A compatibility shim, legacy path or half-finished migration kept instead of a clean migration.
New code re-implements or duplicates an existing primitive, model, helper or tool.
The diff carries unrequested features or unrelated edits, or is far bigger than the ask.
Imprecise types: str for a closed set, Optional on a required field, a missing annotation or exhaustive match.
A silent default, fallback, placeholder or made-up value stands in for data or hides a failure.
The PR text or review guide is miscalibrated: wrong or missing decision flags, unflagged concepts.
A comment, docstring or doc restates code, narrates the edit, points elsewhere, sits at the wrong altitude or should not exist.
Code a reader cannot follow locally: roundabout control flow, unexplained sentinels, long functions.
A test is missing, weak, skipped, trivial, circular or restates the code.
Hardcoded paths, constants, magic values or facts that should be derived or declared once.
A function or tool takes the wrong inputs: paths instead of ids, whole objects, generic passthroughs.
Feature ideas, follow-up requests, housekeeping, performance, security and one-offs.
What LLM-facing text says: role, purpose, procedure, what the model already knows.
